classification.reason: The coach provides executable drills and technical cues such as using an adaptive response drill alternating short and deep feeds, lowering body with knees/hips, and adopting a shallow diagonal Nike swoosh swing.

problem.title_as_question: Why do amateur players brush the ball differently from pros and produce weak, floaty topspin?
problem.definition: Amateur players often try to produce topspin by purely brushing up the back of the ball with their hand or pulling up with level shoulders, resulting in a floaty ball that lacks drive, control, and penetration.
problem.target_player: Intermediate players struggling with floaty, spinny shots that lack depth and pace

symptoms.description: Ball rotates with topspin but produces a floaty, weak trajectory lacking penetration and directional drive
Player abruptly pulls the hand and arm upward with level shoulders instead of driving forward through the ball
Racket dive bombs downward right before contact and attempts a sharp up-and-down timing

causes.statement: Players try to create pure brush rather than driving the racket head through the ball, which disconnects the trunk power from the hand hit.
Players lean back in an attempt to lift the ball instead of leaning in and lowering body height.
Players conceptualize the swing as an exaggerated 'C' shape, dive bombing the racket downward and trying to time a steep down-and-up motion.
The lower body and trunk do not deliver acceleration into the racket head, forcing the player to arm the ball.
Maintaining level shoulders leaves vertical arm pulling as the only way to produce spin, preventing forward penetration.

angles.summary: Even on topspin, the racket must drive through the ball with an incidence angle below horizontal so forward penetration naturally creates upward brush.
The topspin swing path should resemble a shallow Nike swoosh rather than a steep symmetrical C-loop.
Demonstrating that pure brush with level shoulders creates weak floaty balls whereas shoulder slant with a driving path produces penetrating topspin.

solutions.summary: Lower hips and bend knees so the hand does not need to drop artificially low on its own to match the ball height.
When leaning into a ball, get lower with the legs and approach on a slightly lower incidence angle to pick the ball up and down over the net.
Bring the hand close to the level of the ball before forward acceleration to trace a gentle upward diagonal rather than dive bombing.
Oscillate between focusing consciously on the incidence angle cue and hitting with an empty, automatic mind until the cue becomes natural.
Perform the adaptive response drill where feeds alternate pushing deep and pulling forward, requiring heavy spin when leaning back and flatter driving when moving in.
Lean over slightly to create a shoulder slant with a slightly downward racket incidence angle to drive through with topspin.
